narrative.text: The first page of the Russian edition of the WHO note on introducing hepatitis B vaccination into national immunization services, describing the global burden of hepatitis B and the aim of preventing chronic infection. It sets out immunization strategies, including routine infant vaccination as the top priority and a birth dose to prevent perinatal transmission where this is common. The document header is garbled in the OCR.

Covers hepatitis B vaccination priorities where perinatal infection is less common, catch-up vaccination of older people, monovalent and combination vaccine formulations, and schedule options. It notes that the three-dose option with a birth dose is cheaper but harder to administer, while the four-dose option is simpler but more costly and may face supply problems.

Explains how hepatitis B vaccine is injected and that it can be given safely with other vaccines, then describes recommended injection equipment, storage volumes and cold chain requirements. It stresses ensuring a sterile device for every injection and proper disposal of safety boxes.

Covers revising immunization documents and forms, training health staff, choosing between monovalent and combination vaccines, using the vaccine's introduction to strengthen services, and budgeting. It ends with the copyright notice.
